note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: Not acceptable as is. The instruction is clear and states every number; the observation point, level (L1) and family (build) are correct; the gates pass. But the V5 oracle is wrong in both directions. (1) Its start-up check (first 4 output samples <= 0.25) is a requirement the instruction never states, and it rejects a fully correct IIR (Butterworth) high-pass solution that passes every stated behavioural check (verified on the ladder: max_abs 0.70). (2) The stated requirements on the 1 kHz tone and on adding the tones cannot be seen at the single observation point. Flowgraphs that leave out or change the 1 kHz tone pass V5, and three such mutants of the reference survive; with them in the list, the mutation gate would fall to 82%. Minor: the 40 dB check is measured against the 6 kHz output rather than the 1 kHz input, so in-tolerance answers near the boundary are rejected. The task is also a template twin of gbf-dev-04, and it lands in test only because its reference uses an unusual FFT Filter. Fix: add a second File Sink for the filter input, drop the start-up check, add an IIR variant and the low-tone mutants, restate the attenuation as a ratio, and reconsider the split. Scratch work, including the alternative flowgraphs and ladder results, is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-05/.

findings.claim: The oracle has a hidden requirement that rejects a correct IIR high-pass solution. Check 5 (max_abs of the first 4 output samples <= 0.25, described as 'it begins with the filter's start-up from rest') is not stated in the instruction and only holds for FIR filters. Any IIR high-pass (Butterworth, Chebyshev, elliptic) puts out y[0] = b0*x[0] with b0 around 0.3-0.5 and x[0] = 1.5, so its first samples are 0.47-0.73.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-05/alt_iir_butter6.grc: two cos sources (1 kHz amp 1.0, 6 kHz amp 0.5), blocks_add_xx, iir_filter_xxx type ffd with 6th-order Butterworth high-pass taps (cutoff 3 kHz, oldstyle False), File Sink hp_output.dat float. Its 6 kHz gain is 1.0000 and it attenuates 1 kHz by 58.6 dB. `./gb ladder ... --task items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-05/task.json` gives highest V4, first_failed V5. peak_freq 6000 passes, rms 0.353541 passes, band_fraction(1 kHz) 5e-06 passes, band_fraction(6 kHz) 0.999995 passes; only max_abs = 0.700413 > 0.25 fails (result in alt_iir_butter6.result.json). An offline scipy computation of the first 4 outputs gives the same picture: Butterworth order 4/5/6/8 at 0.69/0.64/0.70/0.72, elliptic order 4 at 0.77, Chebyshev II order 6 at 0.62. FIR designs (equiripple optfir, Kaiser firdes.high_pass_2) stay below 0.005. All three accepted variants are FIR, so the variant gate could not catch this. The author's own docstring also notes that a Skip Head after the filter would fail this check.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove check 5 and its spec_property and mutant 3 (tone_hi wired straight to the sink). That mutant stands for an unobservable wiring requirement (see F2); the fix is to observe more, not to add an implementation-specific start-up check. If a start-up check is kept anyway, it must be stated in the instruction, and that would leak the design. Add an IIR variant (hard-coded Butterworth taps) to variants/ so the gate covers this solution class. Note: an Import 'from scipy import signal' clashes with the generated code's own `import signal` (V4 AttributeError), so the variant should use `import scipy.signal as sps` or hard-coded taps.

findings.claim: Several stated requirements are never checked: the 1 kHz tone at peak amplitude 1.0, and adding the two tones before the filter. Flowgraphs that leave out or change the 1 kHz tone pass V5. The declared mutation set leaves out exactly these survivable mutants, so its 100% kill rate overstates what the oracle can tell apart. With those mutants added, the mutation gate would fail (14/17 = 82% < 90%).
findings.evidence: alt_no_low_tone.grc (6 kHz source -> High Pass Filter -> File Sink, no 1 kHz source and no adder) reaches V5 and passes every check (max_abs 0.000593). alt_wrong_low_tone.grc (low tone at 2 kHz, amp 0.05) also passes V5. Mutants applied to reference.grc with edit.apply and run through ladder.check: set_param tone_lo amp 0.05 -> V5 passed; set_param tone_lo freq 2000 -> V5 passed; set_param tone_lo amp 0 -> V5 passed. The instruction states 'one at 1 kHz with a peak amplitude of 1.0' and 'Add the two tones together', and the oracle reads only the filter output, where the 1 kHz tone is gone by design. The authoring rules say every stated behavioural requirement must be checked where measurable. Here it is measurable if a second observation point is added. The build.py docstring admits this as 'known limit (b)', but the claim of a 100% kill rate rests on a mutant list that leaves these cases out.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask in the instruction for the filter input (the two-tone sum) to be written to a second File Sink as well, e.g. tones_sum.dat, item type float. Add checks on that point: peak_freq 1000 Hz, rms sqrt(0.5 + 0.125) = 0.7906 +-5%, band_fraction(900-1100 Hz) about 0.8 and band_fraction(5900-6100 Hz) about 0.2. Add the tone_lo amp/freq mutants and a 'filter fed from tone_hi' mutant to the mutation list, then re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The 1 kHz band_fraction limit (<= 4e-4) measures the 1 kHz residue against the 6 kHz output tone, not against the 1 kHz input as the instruction says ('at least 40 dB weaker at the filter output than at its input'). The limit is derived for a 6 kHz output of exactly 0.5. So an answer whose 6 kHz output is inside its stated tolerance but below 0.5, and which attenuates 1 kHz by between 40.0 and about 40.4 dB, meets the instruction and is rejected. Answers above 0.5 with slightly under 40 dB are accepted.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-05/alt_hamming_gain097.grc: High Pass Filter, Hamming window, cutoff 2350 Hz, width 2050 Hz, gain 0.97. Offline (firdes): 1 kHz attenuation 40.04 dB, 6 kHz amplitude 0.4853 (-2.9%, inside the stated 5%). Ladder: rms 0.343238 passes, but band_fraction(900-1100) = 0.000421 > 0.0004 fails at V5. The ratio does not depend on the filter gain parameter: a1/a6 <= 0.02 is required whatever the gain. At the worst in-tolerance 6 kHz amplitude (0.475), 40 dB attenuation gives about 4.4e-4.
findings.suggested_fix: State the requirement the way it is checked: 'at the output, the 1 kHz component must be at least 34 dB below the 6 kHz tone (its amplitude at most 2 % of the 6 kHz tone's)'. Alternatively, keep the wording and set max to the worst in-tolerance value, 5e-5/(0.475^2/2 + 5e-5) = 4.43e-4, and document the small extra acceptance.

findings.claim: The task's split depends on an arbitrary choice of reference implementation, and the task is a template twin of dev item gbf-dev-04. The natural answer (Signal Sources -> Add -> High Pass Filter -> File Sink) has the signature analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|high_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink, which hashes to dev. The author reached 'test' only by writing the reference with fft_filter_xxx plus a taps variable. That signature is also exactly gbf-dev-04's cluster_id.
findings.evidence: items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-04/task.json: cluster_id 'chain:analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|high_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink'. Its reference sums two float tones (500 Hz amp 0.4 + 60 Hz amp 0.6), high-pass filters to remove the lower tone while keeping the upper tone's amplitude, and writes to a File Sink: the same topology and idea as gbf-test-05, with different numbers. build.py states: 'The more common choice, the High Pass Filter block ... gives a chain that hashes to "dev", so the reference realises the high-pass filter as an FFT Filter'. The eval plan (sec. 6) defines template twins as 'the same flowgraph question for a different signal'. Because the cluster_id comes from the atypical reference, clustered SEs will not group this task with its natural siblings.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not choose the split by changing the reference block. Either move the task to dev, where its natural signature belongs, or give it a different theme or chain whose natural signature hashes to test. At the least, record the gbf-dev-04 twin in review.notes for the team's decision.

compliance.verdict: REFUTED as it stands. The item passes every formal gate, but the oracle is unfair in both directions. Re-running `./gb tier-f gates items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-05` gives the same result as the author: passed, 10/10 solvability, 288 tokens, 3/3 variants, 14 valid mutants all killed. Regenerating with build.py in a scratch copy gives byte-identical task.json, reference.grc and all three variants. The canary GUID appears only in task.json. Licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation and the id/dir/split fields follow the brief. signature_split(reference) is "test". Disjointness from the 62 training-side specs holds: no training spec separates tones by filtering. Four problems survive: (1) Check 5, max_abs of the first 4 output samples ≤ 0.25, encodes a requirement the instruction never states. It rejects correct IIR high-pass answers that meet every stated number. (2) Several wrong answers pass, because the stated 1 kHz amplitude and the 40 dB "relative to its input" requirement cannot be observed. (3) The test split was reached by swapping the filter block id. The natural chain is dev, and is the same template as gbf-dev-04. One accepted variant's chain hashes to train. (4) The run-length (liveness) requirement is unstated, although the sibling build items state it. Scratch evidence is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-05 (make_cands.py, run_cands.py, mut_matrix.py, regen/). The `alt_*` files there were not made by me.

findings.claim: Oracle check 5 (max_abs over the first 4 output samples ≤ 0.25) and its spec_property ('it begins with the filter's start-up from rest') are not in the instruction. They hold only for a linear-phase FIR with small end taps, so correct high-pass designs of another kind fail V5. This breaks the rule that every check maps to a stated requirement.
findings.evidence: Candidate answers in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-05, run with ladder.check against task.json. Each is two cosines (1 kHz amp 1.0, 6 kHz amp 0.5) at 32 kHz, then Add, then iir_filter_xxx (ffd, oldstyle False), then File Sink hp_output.dat. The Butterworth high-pass designs meet every stated number: order 4 / 3.5 kHz gives 44.8 dB at 1 kHz and gain 0.9966 at 6 kHz; order 6 gives 67.2 dB / 0.9997; order 8 gives 89.6 dB / 1.0000; order 5 / 3 kHz designed with scipy.signal.butter in an Import block gives 48.9 dB / 0.9998. All pass checks 1-4 (peak 6000 Hz, rms 0.3524-0.3535, 1 kHz share ≤ 1.3e-4, 6 kHz share ≥ 0.9999). All fail V5 only on check 5: max_abs = 0.626 (order 4), 0.716 (order 6), 0.673 (order 8), 0.635 (order 5, scipy). With sine instead of cosine sources the IIR still fails (0.387 for order 4, 0.257 for order 6). A Skip Head of 200 items after a correct FIR filter also fails (0.463). The author lists the Skip Head case as limit (c) in build.py, but not the IIR case. The mutation matrix shows check 5 is the only check that kills mutant #2 (tone_hi wired straight to the sink: failing checks ['max_abs=0.5']). Every other mutant is killed by checks 1-4.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove check 5 and its spec_property. Mutant #2 then survives, but the kill rate is 13/14 = 92.9%, still at least 90%, so the mutation gate still passes. Record in review.notes that a tone wired straight to the sink cannot be told apart at this observation point. Alternatively, keep a structural check only through an observation point the instruction names, not through a start-up transient.

findings.claim: The oracle cannot observe two stated requirements: the 1 kHz tone has peak amplitude 1.0, and it is 40 dB weaker at the filter output than at the filter input. As a result, clearly wrong answers pass V5.
findings.evidence: These candidates reach V5 and pass: (a) wrong_no_1k_tone.grc has no 1 kHz source and no adder, just 6 kHz source, high_pass_filter, sink (1 kHz share 0.0, rms 0.3537, max_abs 0.0006). (b) wrong_lo_2500.grc puts the lower tone at 2.5 kHz instead of 1 kHz (6 kHz share 0.9931). (c) wrong_lo_amp0p1_rect.grc has the 1 kHz tone at amplitude 0.1 and a rectangular-window filter (cutoff 3 kHz, width 1 kHz) that attenuates 1 kHz by only about 23 dB, violating both the amplitude and the 40 dB requirement. It passes with 1 kHz share 1.96e-4 against max 4e-4. build.py admits limit (b) only in its docstring; task.json gives the team reviewers no sign of it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a second observation point named in the instruction, for example 'also write the sum of the two tones (the filter input) to a File Sink tones_sum.dat, item type float'. Check it for: peak_freq 1000 Hz, rms 0.7906 ± 5 %, band_fraction 900-1100 Hz ≈ 0.8 and 5900-6100 Hz ≈ 0.2. Add the matching mutants: 1 kHz amplitude 0.1, lower tone at 2.5 kHz, 1 kHz source removed. If the team keeps a single observation point, write the limitation into review.notes for the review sheet.

findings.claim: The test split was reached by swapping the filter block id (high_pass_filter to fft_filter_xxx) rather than the task's function. As a result, this test item's own accepted solutions have dev-side and train-side signatures, and the item is a template twin of dev item gbf-dev-04. That defeats the purpose stated in compose.py: 'a test chain is never a template twin of a training chain'.
findings.evidence: signature_split of the variant signatures: v1 (analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|high_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink) is dev; v2 (analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|fir_filter_xxx|blocks_file_sink) is train; v3 (with blocks_throttle2) is test. So the training-side generator, which only has to satisfy signature_split(sig) == 'train', may produce exactly v2's chain: a sum of tones feeding an FIR with high-pass taps into a File Sink. gbf-dev-04 has cluster_id chain:analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|high_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink, the same signature as v1. Its task has the same shape: a wanted tone plus a lower unwanted tone (500 Hz + 60 Hz hum), added, high-pass filtered, written to a File Sink, with checks on upper-tone amplitude and lower-band power share. Eval plan §4.1 and lines 9/20/44 say dev is used for every choice, so tuning on dev-04 transfers directly to this test item. The two items also get different cluster_ids even though they share a template.
findings.suggested_fix: Either move this item to dev (its natural chain is dev), or give the test slot a different function whose natural chain hashes to test. Longer term, normalise filter-implementing block ids (high_pass_filter, fir_filter_xxx, fft_filter_xxx, interp_fir_filter_xxx, iir_filter_xxx, band_pass_filter) to one functional class before signature_split, so the split cannot be reached by swapping a block id. At minimum, note in review.notes that the natural chain is dev and that accepted variant v2's chain is train.

findings.claim: V4 needs at least 16,384 items at hp_output.dat (liveness), but the instruction never says the flowgraph must keep running or produce at least that many samples. A correct answer bounded with a Head block therefore fails, unlike sibling build items that state this requirement.
findings.evidence: head_10000.grc is a correct high-pass answer with a Head of 10,000 items before the File Sink. It fails at V4: "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'out': 10000}". The same answer with Head 32,000 passes V5. Build items gbf-dev-01, gbf-dev-02, gbf-test-02 and gbf-test-04 all say 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' gbf-test-05 does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the instruction: 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.'

findings.claim: The 40 dB requirement is checked as a power share, 1 kHz band ≤ 4.0e-4 of total output power. That threshold assumes the 6 kHz tone is exactly 0.5. Within the stated ±5 % amplitude tolerance, the effective requirement moves by about ±0.45 dB, so an answer at the edge of both stated tolerances can fail.
findings.evidence: With a 6 kHz amplitude of 0.475 (allowed, −5 %) and exactly 40 dB attenuation, the residual 1 kHz power is 5e-5 and the share is 5e-5/(0.1128 + 5e-5) = 4.43e-4, which fails max 4.0e-4; the effective requirement there is 40.45 dB. At 0.525 the check accepts 39.6 dB. build.py's own derivation says the threshold assumes 'upper tone at nominal level'.
findings.suggested_fix: Set max to 4.43e-4, the most lenient value consistent with the stated tolerances, or measure attenuation against the input observation point proposed in F2. At minimum, document the ±0.45 dB coupling in review.notes.
